claims.claim: A generic hero's motivation, a campaign quantity that feeds his battle morale (targeted-02), moves with battles according to his motivation traits, and for two traits taking part alone moves it, whatever the losses or the result. The fan wiki's hero page, as search summaries quote it: Adventurer '+2 when wins a battle in a Foreign Territory +1 after this hero ends a turn in a Province with high Foreign Influence | -2 when Fights a battle in own Territory' (and -1 for ending a turn garrisoned or encamped); Competitive: winning a battle without reinforcements raises it, reinforcing or being reinforced lowers it; Valorous: +1 when it wins a battle, -2 when it loses one. This is the only reference mechanic found in which fighting a battle as such lowers a morale-linked quantity. It is conditional (the trait, the territory, reinforcement) and it acts on one hero's campaign stock, not on every unit that enters.

T5 also named Peaceful, Servile and Sentry traits with a penalty for ending a turn in enemy territory; T10 did not find those names, so they are not claimed. The official 1.7.0 notes confirm that 'motivation traits' exist (targeted-03); faction leaders have no motivation (targeted-02), so this never touches them. INFERRED, untested: the NamuWiki line the community angle could not place ('joining an army' lowering morale by 5 %, community not_found) may be the Competitive dislike of reinforcement. Pattern for our design (D-069): a participation trigger on a commander-level stock, conditional; none of these names or numbers is used.

claims.claim: Motivation is a per-hero stock that reaches a battle through the hero. The fan wiki says it feeds the hero's morale, his rage generation in battle, happiness in the local province and campaign movement range; NamuWiki says high motivation raises the hero's morale and speeds rage recharge in battle, low motivation lowers his morale. Heroes never desert, 'even at -10 motivation'. Faction leaders (Epic Heroes) have no motivation at all. No size of the motivation-to-morale link was found.

claims.claim: The official 1.7.0 notes, as summarised, name 'motivation traits' and fix one: 'Fixed an issue where the motivation traits Hates Trojans and Hates Danaans could be given to Trojan and Danaan heroes respectively'. The same notes make the tutorial's 'Maximum Motivation' mission complete when the player already has a maxed hero. Motivation traits are therefore an official mechanism, limited by side, and motivation has a maximum.

claims.claim: The data holds the structures an event-driven per-hero stock needs, under the engine's name 'loyalty'. This title alone (absent from WARHAMMER II's schema) has 'loyalty_traits_tables', a pool of 'loyalty traits' chosen for characters, each limited by culture and faction. Both titles have 'loyalty_event_effects_tables' (an event, an integer loyalty change, a loyalty factor, a percentage chance, a threshold) and a junction by which effects modify loyalty events. This title alone adds 'xp_gain_mod_from_loyalty' (XP gain scaled by character loyalty) and 'minimum_loyalty_ai_faction'. The word 'motivation' occurs nowhere in the schema. INFERRED: motivation is character loyalty under another name, and its battle triggers (fighting, winning, losing, being reinforced) are loyalty events whose changes the motivation traits set. If so, motivation also raises the XP a hero gains.

claims.claim: This title's campaign AI is defined to read a per-army morale on the campaign map. A task-management table found only in this title's schema (none of its keys occurs in WARHAMMER II's) sets two thresholds on 'a forces morale' on a 0.0 to 1.0 scale: a force is released to aggressive tasks outside its faction's territory only above one, and is forced to return from such tasks below the other. Each is paired with a size threshold in units (1 to 20). What that morale level is computed from (the inherited military-force morale family, data-14, or an estimate of the army's condition), its values, and whether the player ever sees it are NOT established.

not_found: Q1 (reference), this angle's addition: 24 searches phrased in the game's interface terms (the morale tooltip's lines such as 'flanks secure', 'fighting outnumbered', 'army losses' and 'surprised'; units 'wavering' at deployment; a 'surprise attack' or ambush at the start; a second battle in the same turn; victory and defeat effects lasting turns; campaign-AI morale) found NO source for a morale cost of entering a battle, or of simply being in one, at either level, nor for a unit deploying below its base value (search log T1-T24). With the earlier angles (official not_found, community-01, data-01): on the evidence found, the reference neither supports nor contradicts D-083 DB1, and no source shows that it charges every unit for entering. The nearest mechanics are conditional: a hero's motivation lowered merely by fighting in his own territory or by being reinforced, for two traits (targeted-01); start-of-battle fatigue set on the campaign map (official-01 to official-05); terms that act without losses, such as surprise, night unpreparedness, exposed flanks and nearby enemy numbers (data-02, data-04). This is an absence in search summaries, not proof.

Q1/Q8 (reference): the size of the motivation-to-morale link; whether it reaches the hero's army or only his own unit; the full list of motivation traits, and whether any trait dislikes fighting a battle anywhere (not only in own territory).

Q2 (reference): what NamuWiki's 'joining an army' morale penalty (community not_found) refers to; one candidate, the Competitive trait's dislike of reinforcement (targeted-01), is INFERRED and untested.

Q3, Q4, Q6, Q7 (reference): nothing beyond the earlier angles. No value of any battle-morale term except the mod author's 90 s charge window (targeted-07); no rally rule, shatter count or post-rally value beyond community-12; no morale penalty for the ambushed side (T1: 'The results didn't cover surprise attacks'; T2: no source for an ambush or surprise penalty at deployment); no fatigue-to-morale size; no morale carried from one battle to a second in the same turn (T3).
